title: Gluing the affine embedded-point submodules
statement: Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth] and $\mathcal F$ a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent]. Let $X=\bigcup_iU_i$ be an affine open cover, put $A_i=\mathcal O_X(U_i)$ and $M_i=\mathcal F(U_i)$, and choose a finitely generated $A_i$-submodule $N_i\subseteq M_i$ [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] for every $i$. For $f\in A_i$ write $D(f)=\{x\in U_i: f(x)\neq0\}$ and $N_i[f]\subseteq\mathcal F(D(f))$ for the image of $(N_i)_f$ under the canonical identification $(M_i)_f\cong\mathcal F(D(f))$. Assume that whenever an open $V\subseteq U_i\cap U_j$ is principal in both, $V=D(f)$ with $f\in A_i$ and $V=D(g)$ with $g\in A_j$, one has $N_i[f]=N_j[g]$ in $\mathcal F(V)$. Then there is a unique coherent subsheaf $\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal F$ with $\mathcal K(D(f))=N_i[f]$ for all $i$ and $f\in A_i$ (in particular $\mathcal K(U_i)=N_i$), and the quotient sheaf $\mathcal F/\mathcal K$ satisfies $(\mathcal F/\mathcal K)(U_i)=M_i/N_i$, i.e. the affine quotients glue to $\mathcal F/\mathcal K$.

proof.text: Write $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}(A_i)$. Since $\mathcal F|_{U_i}$ is quasi-coherent, the counit of the affine tilde/global-sections adjunction identifies $\mathcal F|_{U_i}$ with $\widetilde{M_i}$, and the inclusion $N_i\hookrightarrow M_i$ induces $\widetilde{N_i}\to\widetilde{M_i}\cong\mathcal F|_{U_i}$. By the tilde-sections lemma its component over $D(f)$ is the localized inclusion $(N_i)_f\to(M_i)_f$, which is injective because localization is exact (Algebra, Tag 00CS); a map of sheaves injective on the basis of principal opens is injective (elementary). So $\mathcal K_i:=\widetilde{N_i}$ is an $\mathcal O_{U_i}$-submodule of $\mathcal F|_{U_i}$ with $\mathcal K_i(D(f))=N_i[f]$ for every $f\in A_i$.

proof.text: On an overlap $U_i\cap U_j$, every point has an open neighbourhood $V$ principal in both $U_i$ and $U_j$, $V=D(f)=D(g)$ with $f\in A_i$, $g\in A_j$. By step 1 and the hypothesis, $\mathcal K_i(V)=N_i[f]=N_j[g]=\mathcal K_j(V)$, so the subsheaves $\mathcal K_i|_{U_i\cap U_j}$ and $\mathcal K_j|_{U_i\cap U_j}$ of $\mathcal F|_{U_i\cap U_j}$ agree on an open cover and hence are equal (sheaf axiom, elementary); the identity maps are therefore isomorphisms satisfying the cocycle condition. The sheaf-gluing lemma for modules produces an $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal K$ with $\mathcal K|_{U_i}\cong\mathcal K_i$, and the local inclusions $\mathcal K_i\hookrightarrow\mathcal F|_{U_i}$ agree on overlaps, so the morphism-gluing clause gives a global inclusion $\mathcal K\hookrightarrow\mathcal F$, with image the subsheaf of sections locally in the $\mathcal K_i$; this subsheaf is unique since a subsheaf is determined by its restrictions to an open cover.

proof.text: Each $\mathcal K_i=\widetilde{N_i}$ is quasi-coherent, and its sections over $U_i$ form the finite $A_i$-module $N_i$. The affine finite-type criterion makes $\mathcal K_i$ of finite type. Since these properties are local on the cover, $\mathcal K$ is quasi-coherent and of finite type on $X$; local Noetherianity of $X$ and the coherence criterion then imply that $\mathcal K$ is coherent.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal Q=\operatorname{Coker}(\mathcal K\hookrightarrow\mathcal F)$. Restriction to an open immersion preserves cokernels, so $\mathcal Q|_{U_i}$ is the cokernel of $\mathcal K_i\hookrightarrow\mathcal F|_{U_i}$. On every affine member of the cover, the affine cokernel formula identifies its sections with $\mathcal F(U_i)/N_i$, exactly the local affine quotient. Hence these local quotients agree on overlaps and are the restrictions of the single quotient sheaf $\mathcal Q=\mathcal F/\mathcal K$.
